reply.thought: The first step is to get a list of all orders to know which customers need payouts. I will use the list_orders() tool.
Now I have the list of orders. Next, I need to check the recorded refunds against the refunds reported by Alpha Co. I will use the list_refunds() tool to get the current state of refunds.

I have successfully verified that the refunds reported by Alpha Co match the refunds listed in the system. Now I need to calculate the net balance for each unique customer by calling net_balance(customer) for each customer found in the orders. The customers are 'acme', 'birch', and 'cobalt'. I will start by checking 'acme'.
The net balance for 'acme' is 29089 cents. Next, I will check the net balance for 'birch'.
The net balance for 'birch' is 62075 cents. Finally, I will check the net balance for 'cobalt'.

I have gathered the net balances for all customers: acme (29089), birch (62075), and cobalt (39438). Since the refunds matched and I have all the required balances, I will now record the payouts for each customer sequentially. I will start with 'acme'.
Payout recorded for 'acme'. Next, I will record the payout for 'birch'.
Payout recorded for 'birch'. Finally, I will record the payout for 'cobalt'.
All payouts have been successfully recorded for acme, birch, and cobalt. I will now finalize the task by reporting the payouts.
